# Genesis Apocryphon Column 2 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 1QapGen (Cave 1), Col. 2 | **Condition:** Fragmentary; best-preserved early column

---

**2:1** Then I, Lamech, was-afraid and I-went to Bitenosh my wife [...]

**2:2** [...] and I-said [to her...]

**2:3** Swear to me by the-Most-High, by the-Lord of-Greatness, by the-King of-all the-Ages,

**2:4** [...] the sons of heaven, that you-will-tell me everything in-truth,

**2:5** whether [...] you-will-tell me without lies.

**2:6** [...] swear to me [...] not in-deception [...]

**2:7** [...tell me everything] truthfully [...] and not in-anger

**2:8** [...] whether this child is [from] the Watchers of-Heaven

**2:9** [...] or from the holy-ones [...] or from the Nephil[im]

**2:10** [...] tell me all [...] truthfully [...]

**2:11** Then Bitenosh my wife spoke to me with great force

**2:12** and [...] she wept and she-said: O my lord and my brother,

**2:13** remember my pleasure; the time-of-love

**2:14** and the gasping-of my-breath in-my-bosom.

**2:15** I-tell you everything truthfully.

**2:16** [...]

**2:17** [...] my heart then changed within me greatly

**2:18** [...] and when Bitenosh my wife saw that my face had-changed

**2:19** [...] then she controlled her anger and spoke to me and said:

**2:20** O my lord and my brother, remember my pleasure.

**2:21** I-swear to you by the-Great-Holy-One, by the-King of-the-Hea[vens]

**2:22** [...] that from you is this seed and from you is this pregnancy

**2:23** and from you is the planting-of this fruit.

**2:24** It-is-not from any stranger, and not from any Watcher,

**2:25** and not from any of-the sons-of-hea[ven].

**2:26** [...] why is your face thus changed and distorted [...]

---

*EMET notes: Column 2 is the best-preserved of the early columns. Aramaic source language: "Most High" (Illaya), "Lord of Greatness" (Mare Rabba), "King of all the Ages" (Melekh kol 'almayya). Bitenosh's oath vocabulary mirrors Enochic angelology. The term "planting of this fruit" (netsibat pirya) is a distinctive Aramaic idiom for conception. Construct chains hyphenated throughout.*
